newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine tycoon rejects "Al Capone" murder link.
newsitem.headline: Argentine tycoon rejects "Al Capone" murder link.

text.p: A businessman accused of being the godfather of organised crime in Argentina on Tuesday dismisssed "ridiculous theories" linking him to the murder of a news photographer and saying he had government protection.

Postal tycoon Alfredo Yabran, named by ex-Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo and opposition leaders as "the head of the mafia," took out a full-page advertisement in major newspapers to reject allegations that "put me in the role of Al Capone."
Yabran and his personal security chief appeared in court on Friday to give evidence in the January murder of Noticias news magazine photographer Jose Luis Cabezas.

Cabezas, 35, was handcuffed, beaten and shot in the head, his body doused with fuel and burned beyond recognition. The gruesome crime brought back memories of the 1970s death squads and sparked public outrage and mass protests.
The newsman's body was exhumed on Tuesday for a second autopsy to determine whether he was shot once or twice.

The arrest of a former policeman, Gustavo Prellezo, for allegedly shooting Cabezas, and the hunt for whoever ordered the murder, has taken on strong political overtones and the case has continued to grab front-page headlines.

Yabran and his security man Gregorio Rios were questioned about phone calls Prellezo made to Yabran's home in the days before the murder. Prosecutor Maria Elena Brignoles said they might now be called for questioning rather than as witnesses.
"I was not at all convinced by Rios' explanations of the telephone calls," Brignoles told reporters.

Investigators were looking into links between Prellezo and Yabran's security staff and into Noticias' articles on Yabran, which included photographs of the camera-shy businessman and his wife on the beach, taken by Cabezas.
But the silver-haired Yabran dismissed "ridiculous theories about a faithful employee wishing to please his boss (by) killing someone in revenge for a photo on a beach."
Yabran said his accusers were trying to advance their political careers or remove him from competition in imminent privatisations of the state post office and airports.
Cavallo said Yabran enjoys the protection of government ministers and accused President Carlos Menem, who has denied reports he is a friend of Yabran, of being "afraid" of him.
Yabran said in his ad that he was "one of the people most eager" to have the Cabezas case solved "without subordination to commercial interests or premeditated political campaigns."
"Because if that doesn't happen, then we certainly would have become a mafia society," he said.
